source.acip: `GNYIS PA RANG LUGS BZHAG PA LA, BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG LA, LAS CAN GYI LHA MI YI DVAGS GSUM GYIS CIG CAR DU BLTAS PA DE'I TSE, CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE DNGOS PO GSUM GYI GZHI MTHUN PA MA YIN PA DANG , DE'I TSE TSAD MTSUNGS GSUM NGES PAR MI DGOS SHING , BRLAN ZHING GSHER BA CHU PHOR PA GANG PO DE CHA SHAS GSUM LDAN DU SKYE BA DANG ,
source.wylie: `gnyis pa rang lugs bzhag pa la, brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang la, las can gyi lha mi yi dvags gsum gyis cig car du bltas pa de'i tshe, chu phor pa gang po de dngos po gsum gyi gzhi mthun pa ma yin pa dang , de'i tshe tshad mtshungs gsum nges par mi dgos shing , brlan zhing gsher ba chu phor pa gang po de cha shas gsum ldan du skye ba dang
source.english: Here secondly is the section where we establish our own position. Now suppose three different types of beings--a pleasure being, a human, and a craving spirit, each with their own karma--sit down together and look upon a glass filled with water, the thing we define as "wet and flowing." The glass of water is not at this point one thing which is simultaneously three different objects. Neither is it necessary in this situation for there to be three identical valid perceptions. And when the glass full of wet and flowing water occurs, it occurs with three different, distinct parts to it.
